title: Sell, serve and stay safe with WhatsApp Business

say: Sell, serve and stay safe with WhatsApp Business.
This is the video for module four of WhatsApp for Communication and Business.
WhatsApp Business is a free app made for small businesses. Your customers chat with you from their normal WhatsApp.

say: Step one. Install WhatsApp Business from the Play Store or App Store, developer WhatsApp LLC. It is free. Anyone selling a blue tick or activation is not from WhatsApp.

say: Step two. Use a separate business SIM if you can, so family chats stay private. If customers already know your number, back up first, then verify that number in the Business app and it offers to move your chats.

say: Open Business tools, Business profile. Start with your logo on a plain background, or a clear shop photo.

say: For the description use this formula: what you offer, who it is for, where or how, and one action. For example, handmade shea butter creams for dry skin, delivery in Abuja, tap Catalog to order.

say: The catalogue is your shop window. Use clear daylight photos on a plain background. Prices change often, so update them, or write Price on request.

say: A greeting message goes automatically to new customers. Keep it to three or four short lines with one action. Set the away message to Outside of business hours, never Always send, or customers think you are never available.

say: Rose sells phone accessories in Computer Village, Ikeja. A buyer orders goods worth 38,000 naira, arrives, shows a transfer screenshot and says, please hurry, my driver is waiting.

panel.heading: A fake credit alert at the counter
items: Buyer shows a screenshot and rushes her
Pressure is a red flag
She checks her own Moniepoint app
No money: goods stay; report and block

say: Rose notices the pressure. That is a red flag.

panel.heading: A fake credit alert at the counter
items: Buyer shows a screenshot and rushes her
Pressure is a red flag
She checks her own Moniepoint app
No money: goods stay; report and block

say: She opens her own Moniepoint app to check incoming transfers. No payment of 38,000 naira has arrived.

panel.heading: A fake credit alert at the counter
items: Buyer shows a screenshot and rushes her
Pressure is a red flag
She checks her own Moniepoint app
No money: goods stay; report and block

say: She politely says goods are released only when the money shows. The buyer leaves. Rose reports and blocks the number, and adds that rule to her slash pay quick reply.

panel.rule: Release goods only when money reflects in YOUR banking app.

say: Three rules stop most scams. Never share your six-digit code or two-step PIN.
Never release goods or refunds until money reflects in your own banking app.
And if a new number with a relative's photo asks for urgent money, call that person on a number you already know.

panel.heading: Three rules, every time
items: Never share your six-digit code or PIN
Release goods only after money reflects
Verify urgent money requests by calling

say: To remember. Use a business SIM and turn on two-step verification. Fill a complete, truthful profile. Switch on your catalogue, greeting, quick replies and labels. And always check payments in your own app, never by screenshot.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Separate business SIM and two-step verification
Complete, truthful profile with real hours
Catalogue, greeting, quick replies, labels
Check payments in your own app

say: Now set up your shop. Fill every profile field, add five products to your catalogue, create four quick replies, and update your payment reply with the rule.
Then continue with the lessons below.

panel.heading: Your practice tasks
items: Fill every business profile field
